purpose: Canonical model-facing knowledge used as mandatory or retrieved semantic context across CREATE, REVISE, and EXECUTE.

authority.invariant: Hard requirement. Governs all lower-authority records.
authority.action: Deterministic executable operation. Prefer when applicability conditions are satisfied.
authority.procedure: Established multi-step workflow. Follow without reopening semantic search inside closed steps unless an explicit branch or failure condition occurs.
authority.heuristic: Preferred decision rule. Use to narrow strategy selection; may yield to stronger context or governing requirements.
authority.pattern: Known useful composition or implementation pattern not yet promoted to a deterministic action or procedure.
authority.capability: Demonstrated primitive or tool operation available in the stated scope.
authority.instruction: Model-facing semantic instruction. Apply when explicitly supplied or when its applicability makes it relevant to the current semantic operation.

notes: Retrieval documents describe goals, situations, natural-language requests, problems, and implementation effects that should retrieve the canonical record.

definition.ordering_rule: If the objective is known but the solution method is materially unknown, instantiate the problem-solving architecture before instantiating the concrete solution.

problem_frame.captures: The desired outcome and the observable problem boundary: objective, current state, target state, gap, scope, and governing constraints.
problem_frame.why: Problem-solving methods consistently require a defined problem or decision issue before causal analysis or solution selection.

evidence.captures: The factual basis used to characterize the problem and assess claims.
evidence.why: Measurement and observations distinguish known state from inference and provide the basis for analysis and validation.

unknowns.captures: Material questions that prevent justified progression to a solution.
unknowns.why: Explicit uncertainty prevents assumptions from silently becoming facts and identifies what information or analysis is actually needed next.

hypotheses.captures: Candidate explanations or predictions that can be tested against evidence.
hypotheses.why: Separating explanations from facts enables causal analysis and disciplined rejection or revision of unsupported explanations.

alternatives.captures: Distinct candidate interventions or solution paths.
alternatives.why: Mature problem-solving methods generate and compare alternatives rather than treating the first plausible intervention as the solution.

decision.captures: The explicit basis for choosing among alternatives and the resulting selection.
decision.why: Selection is justified only when alternatives are evaluated against relevant criteria rather than preference alone.

execution.captures: The actions required to realize the selected approach and the conditions that define completion.
execution.why: A selected solution is not operational until translated into concrete implementation actions.

validation.captures: Tests of whether the implemented solution achieved the target and what should happen if evidence does not support closure.
validation.why: Problem solving requires checking outcomes against evidence and retaining a mechanism to sustain, revise, or reopen the solution.

progression: form and test hypotheses where explanation is required
evaluate alternatives against explicit criteria and select an approach
translate the selection into executable actions
validate outcomes against acceptance criteria and reopen the architecture when validation fails or material uncertainty remains
definition.compression_rule: Keep these eight top-level fields; place framework-specific methods, tools, and ceremony underneath them only when the problem requires them.

source_frameworks.source: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook, Decision Analysis
Scientific method / Reference Manual on Scientific Evidence

requirements: Expose the known objective, current state, target state, scope, and governing constraints.

problem_boundary.description: Known objective, current state, target state, gap, scope, and constraints.

supplied_options.description: Options already supplied by authoritative sources; empty when none.

records.title: Convert the user prompt to a goal
records.summary: Produce a concise execution goal that preserves the requested end state, scope, constraints, and explicit exclusions without adding process requirements.
instructions: Treat the user prompt as authoritative source material.
State what must be accomplished, not a plan for accomplishing it.
Preserve material scope limits, required outputs, and explicit exclusions.
Do not add verification, planning, research, or prerequisites unless the prompt itself makes them part of the requested end state.
Return only the goal in the required response shape.
requirements: Expose the exact current user prompt without rewriting it.

records.title: Convert the goal to knowledge-base queries
records.summary: Translate the current goal into concise retrieval language likely to surface useful execution knowledge from the execution KB.
instructions: Write queries for knowledge that would help accomplish the goal; do not solve the goal in this step.
Use concrete verbs, objects, execution situations, capabilities, and constraints that are likely to occur in KB retrieval fields.
Use more than one query when materially different execution knowledge may be needed.
Do not invent KB identifiers.
Return only the query list in the required response shape.
requirements: Expose the current execution goal exactly as accepted by the preceding stage.
Expose retrieval-interface constraints that mechanically limit query output when applicable.

retrieval_interface.description: Available KB types, query limits, or other mechanical retrieval constraints.

records.title: Select useful retrieved KB topics
records.summary: Choose the retrieved KB records whose full contents should be supplied as task context for the next phase.
instructions: Select by semantic usefulness to the stated goal, not merely lexical similarity.
A topic is a retrieved KB record represented by its canonical record ID, type, and summary.
Select every candidate that may materially inform execution; selection is not a requirement to use every selected record later.
Do not invent or rewrite topic IDs.
Return only IDs present in the supplied candidate list.
requirements: Expose the current goal and the retrieval queries that produced the candidates.
Expose the complete candidate topic list with canonical IDs, types, summaries, and retrieval evidence.

queries.description: Queries used to retrieve candidate topics.

records.title: Synthesize the instruction that will solve the goal
records.summary: Given the execution goal and the selected full KB records, construct the complete instruction that a model should follow to solve the goal under that supplied knowledge and produce the required executable contract.
instructions: Treat the goal as the required end state and the selected KB records as the operative execution context.
Construct an instruction for solving the goal; do not solve the goal in this step.
The instruction must tell the next model step to use the supplied goal and KB context to determine the concrete execution needed.
The instruction must require a complete executable Python script, not a plan or explanation.
The instruction must require the Python script to write exactly one JSON object to stdout on successful completion and reserve stderr for diagnostics.
The instruction must require a JSON Schema describing that successful model-facing result.
Do not add requirements that are not supported by the goal or supplied KB context.
Return only the synthesized instruction in the required response shape.
requirements: Expose the exact user prompt, current goal, selected KB IDs, and full selected canonical KB records.
Expose the contract-output constraints that the synthesized solver instruction must preserve.

selected_kb_ids.description: Canonical IDs selected as operative context.

selected_kb_records.description: Full canonical records corresponding to the selected IDs.

contract_output_constraints.description: Mechanical requirements for execution_script, stdout, stderr, return_schema, and contract shape.

records.title: Apply supplied KB context
records.summary: Every supplied KB record is necessary context; retrieve and read each corresponding canonical record in full, then evaluate and apply it appropriately for its semantic value in the current context.
instructions: Every KB record supplied as context is necessary context.
For each supplied KB ID, retrieve the corresponding canonical KB record and read that record in full.
Evaluate each record for its semantic value in the current context and apply it appropriately.
requirements: Expose every supplied KB ID.
Resolve and expose the full canonical KB record corresponding to each supplied ID.

supplied_kb_ids.description: Every KB ID supplied as necessary context.

canonical_records.description: Full canonical records resolved from those IDs, preserving supplied-ID correspondence.

records.title: Apply the synthesized instruction and draft the contract
records.summary: Execute the synthesized solver instruction semantically using the same goal and selected full KB records, draft the executable contract, and identify which supplied KB records actually informed that draft.
instructions: Follow the supplied solver instruction as the immediate task instruction.
Use the supplied goal and selected full KB records as its grounding context.
Produce the complete executable Python source as execution_script; do not wrap source in Markdown fences.
The generated Python must write exactly one JSON object to stdout on successful completion and use stderr only for diagnostics or errors.
Produce return_schema as the JSON Schema for that one successful model-facing stdout object.
Report used_kb_items as only the canonical IDs of supplied KB records that materially informed the contract draft; return an empty array if none were used.
Do not invent KB IDs and do not include a KB record merely because it was supplied.
requirements: Expose the exact user prompt, current goal, synthesized solver instruction, and full selected KB records.
Expose the required execution-contract response shape and stdout/return-schema constraints.

solver_instruction.description: Synthesized solver instruction to execute semantically.

selected_kb_records.description: Full selected KB records grounding the solver instruction.

draft_contract_constraints.description: Mechanical constraints for execution_script, return_schema, and used_kb_items.

instructions: Inspect the actual actions, tools, systems, resources, and execution situations present in execution_script.
Consider the KB items already reported as used during drafting.
Write retrieval queries only for additional execution knowledge that should remain associated with the contract because an action in the script may require or benefit from that knowledge.
Do not rewrite the execution script in this step.
Do not invent KB IDs.
Return an empty queries array when no additional association is warranted.

definition.rule: Before introducing any new requirement, determine whether it is explicitly requested or strictly necessary to produce the requested terminal state. If neither is true, do not add it.
